notes.title: “SaGa Frontier 2 Remastered” launches today!
notes.content:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2452080/

“SaGa Frontier 2”, originally released in 1999, has launched today as a HD remaster!

This version not only features high resolution graphics, but also a restructured UI and a brushed-up game system, including the addition of the ability to inherit growth parameters, making the game fully enjoyable both for those that played the SaGa series in the past and now for the first time.

The game also includes new historical scenes untold in the original game, as well as new characters that can engage in battles, allowing players to enjoy the storyline even more deeply.

A new “SaGa Frontier 2” is here, evolved to be much easier to learn and play!

notes.title: Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven Available Today!
notes.content:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2455640/

This game is a full remake of Romancing SaGa 2, the classic RPG from 1993 that sold a million copies in Japan.

The original game has been rebuilt with numerous accessibility updates to make it an exciting and enjoyable experience for SaGa series veterans and complete newcomers alike.

[b]■Story[/b]
Seven heroes saved the world in ages past, but the ancients feared their power and exiled them to another dimension.
Thousands of years have elapsed since The Seven were banished, and they have long passed into legend, but it was always said that they would return one day to save the world again.
Finally, they appear once more, but none can say what fate the heroes return will herald…

[b]■Imperial Succession[/b]
The player becomes the Emperors of Avalon and works to expand the realm while battling against the Seven Heroes. To stand against the incredible might of these foes, successive Emperors must pass their powers down the line of succession to their descendants and engage in an epic conflict that spans millennia. 

[b]■Characters[/b]
Over 30 different classes, featuring a plethora of races and occupations.
Each class has its own unique capabilities, favoured weapons and magical powers.
Characters from any class can ascend to become emperor.



[h3]Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven Demo available now![/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45065531/45ddb5a444af8cd2c63d3c774a37dd0016125964.png[/img]
The demo lets you enjoy the opening chapter of the game, where Emperor Leon and his comrades take on Kzinssie of the Seven Heroes. Story progress from the demo can be carried over to the full game.

This remake keeps the epic story of the war fought between the imperial line of Varennes and the Seven Heroes of legend, as well as all the unique mechanics from the SaGa franchise, such as “Glimmers” and “Formations” while reworking the battle and character growth systems and adding numerous new features such as JP and EN voice acting. notes.title: A Message from the Developers
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790790/87fa14d233d9e88d7557887036b93ae6746dc7c5.jpg[/img]
[b]FORGE YOUR OWN TALE[/b]
The latest standalone entry in the SaGa franchise, SaGa Emerald Beyond brings together the very best elements of the beloved series to offer each player their own unique gameplay experience. Choose from five sets of lead characters and weave your own tale through 17 different worlds.
The full game is finally available today!
 
To celebrate the launch of the game, the SaGa Emerald Beyond developers came together to answer some of the communities hottest question in an interview style Q&A. 

[b]Is there any connection between the characters and setting of SaGa Emerald Beyond and past SaGa games?[/b] 
Series mainstays such as Glimmers and United Attacks are still present in SaGa Emerald Beyond, but there’s no connection in terms of the story and setting. Having said that, there might be some places that hit a little harder if you’ve played a title from the SaGa series before.
 
[b]Can you still enjoy SaGa Emerald Beyond without having played any other SaGa games?[/b] 
Yes - since there’s no connection to other titles in the series, you don’t need to have played any other SaGa games to enjoy Emerald Beyond.
There’s a demo available as well, so in case you’re unsure about this type of game, you could to start by playing the demo first.
 
[b]Which protagonist would you recommend for newcomers to the SaGa franchise, and which would you recommend for experts?[/b] 
Tsunanori Mido is fairly easy to get to grips with if you are new to all the different systems of SaGa. 
Whereas Bonnie and Formina might be more fun to play if you are already well versed in the series or after you’ve explored lots of different worlds with the other characters of SaGa Emerald Beyond, but if you like a challenge, of course there’s no problem with picking them first! 
 
[b]Do you have any tips for the battles?[/b]
The trick to having a successful battle is to connect the combo range of each individual tech.
In the beginning, just focus on trying to connect the green lines above all else. On top of that, it’s also important to try and disrupt enemy United Attacks.
 
[b]What kind of play time should I expect?[/b]
Starting with either of the 5 sets of protagonists, it takes a good few hours - around 10 - to reach your very first ending.
Each of the lead characters has a vastly different story and we developed the game in a way that you will never experience exactly the same thing twice. The story and ending will be different for each player, each playthrough - so play time can basically be infinite!
 
[b]Are you planning any DLC?[/b]
We don’t have any plans for DLC - but rest assured, there’s already plenty of content in SaGa Emerald Beyond.

With this we hope that you will be excited to dive into the divers worlds of SaGa Emerald Beyond. May your adventure be guided by the Emerald Wave!

notes.title: The wait is over! Saga Emerald Beyond is available now!
notes.content:
Make use of glimmers and combos in battle; meet a diverse cast of races, including monsters, mechs, and vampires; and experience your very own story, created through your choices and actions.

[b]Distant Worlds Woven Together:[/b]
Travel to 17 unique worlds from the Junction, either led by the hand of destiny or by a path forged by your own choices.
Discover the completely different cultures and landscapes, ranging from a densely developed forest of skyscrapers and a green and luscious habitat covered in plant life to a world governed by five witches, or one ruled by vampires - just to name a few of the distinct settings.

[b]An Eclectic Cast of Protagonists:[/b]
Six leading characters, all from diverse backgrounds and with vastly different goals, set out on their journey in five unique story arcs.
They venture to the myriad of worlds for their very own personal reasons: One, a human on a mission to protect the barrier defending his city; another, a witch trying to regain her lost magic while maintaining her disguise as a schoolgirl; and yet another, a vampire lord out to regain his crown and reclaim the throne as the rightful king of his world.
Even selecting the same protagonist for a second--or third or fourth--playthrough will lead to completely new events and stories, a completely fresh path and experience.

[b]TSUNANORI MIDO[/b]
A man who can manipulate kugutsu, animated puppets which bear their own will, and is tasked with protecting the barrier around his city! To achieve this Tsunanori is selected for the Cathedral Project to investigate other worlds and restore order to the spiritual realm.

[b]AMEYA AISLING[/b]
An up-and-coming witch who has hidden her true form under the guise of an elementary school girl! Determined to get her magical powers back, after losing them through an attack by an unknown man, and pass her witchterms, Ameya ventures out with her cat familiar LoLo.

[b]SIUGNAS[/b]
An immortal vampire who rules over a world shrouded in darkness, as the Dismal King! Betrayed and driven from his throne, when he awakens, Siugnas sets out on a journey to recover his powers, accompanied by the other warriors in his squadron.

[b]DIVA NO. 5[/b]
A mech designed to be the perfect entertainer! Capturing the hearts of all those who saw her perform, one day a forbidden song causes her memory and singing functionality to be sealed away. In her despair, Diva discards her “human” body and joins a secret society, leaving everything she had known behind.
And did you know, if you started Diva's journey in the free Steam Demo, you'll be able to carry your progress across to the full release?

[b]BONNIE BLAIR & FORMINA FRANKLYN[/b]
Two new recruits on the police force, investigating an assassination attempt! Former marine Bonnie, and renowned sharpshooter Formina set off on a journey together through the other worlds, to uncover the hidden truth behind the incident. 

[b]A Story of Your Very Own Making:[/b]
SaGa Emerald Beyond has the greatest number of branching plots of any game in the SaGa series.
The story branches abundantly depending on your choices and actions. Every time you visit a world, the story will evolve, allowing the protagonist and player alike to discover new possibilities.
As the story unfolds in this way it becomes a tale all of your own, not only affecting the path you walk but also the multiple potential endings that await each protagonist.

[b]Battles where a Single Choice Can Change Everything:[/b]
SaGa Emerald Beyond further refines the highly strategic Timeline Battles the SaGa franchise has been long renowned for. With series mainstays such as the skill to spontaneously acquire abilities through the Glimmer system, tactical ally placement known as Formations, and United Attacks that enable individual skills to connect together to form devastating chain attacks, it offers the best iteration of SaGa's turn-based combat to date.

The new combat system adds more drama than ever before, allowing you to support party members, interrupt enemy actions, and use United Attacks by strategically manipulating the order of ally actions.

The characters that join you, the weapons you wield, your party formation, and your tactics in battle - everything is up to you!

notes.title: SaGa Frontier Remastered (Switch) Review
notes.content:
[img]https://www.cgmagonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/SaGa-Frontier-Remastered-Switch-Review.jpg[/img]

SaGa Frontier Remastered is a game about discovery and exploration.

That’s a simple, perhaps even positive, way to describe how it leaves you to your own devices to figure out how nearly everything in the game actually works. From how to advance the story to how to learn new skills, few things in SaGa Frontier Remastered are explained, fewer still are elaborated upon, and you will learn through repeated experimentation and failures.

Sometimes, this open structure works against it. But I couldn’t help but be captivated by it.

Originally released in 1997, SaGa Frontier is one of many weird RPGs released during the PlayStation era that sought to experiment with the genre’s conventions. In this case, that meant the ‘Free Scenario System’, wherein you chose one of seven playable characters that each had their own narrative that was set amongst a disparate collection of worlds.

The protagonists are a diverse bunch, each with wildly different stories to follow. Emilia is a former model who was wrongfully imprisoned for the murder of her fiancé and is now searching for the real culprit. Blue is a young mage who searches for magic while preparing for a future fight against his twin, the winner of whom will receive sacred magic. T260 is a robot that must recover its memory and complete its secret mission. Some characters’ stories are linear, others more open in design, but each has the freedom to explore the entire world after a short introduction, allowing you to uncover new party members, quests, and occasionally new endings.

While I found most of the stories interesting, they are told with a surprising amount of brevity that frequently left me wanting more. Dialogue is short and clipped all around, with few interactions between characters. Often, you’ll be wondering what exactly you have to do next. There is a story section in the menu that summarizes what is going on but following it too closely will leave you unprepared for new areas because it ignores the element that makes SaGa Frontier Remastered shine — exploration.

The lack of instruction in SaGa Frontier forces you to discover nearly everything along your journey, be it new locations to new battle mechanics. This focus is at times frustrating — I would have loved to have known how to earn new skills earlier than I did, for example — but without it, I would not have come to learn as much as I did about the world and its systems. Discovering new party members in some random corner of the world, finding out the best ways to make money, slowly traversing a ruin not knowing what’s on the other side; these are the moments that made me appreciate the lack of instruction.

Nowhere is that better demonstrated than in the battle system. Combat is turn-based, with a variety of attacks and spells to choose from. There is no traditional experience or level up system, as stats and abilities are improved by repeatedly performing certain actions. Skills, to answer my earlier anecdote, are earned randomly mid-battle when facing tougher enemies and fulfilling unexplained conditions. Human, robot, and monster party members all feature different mechanics to get used to. In a word, combat is dense.

Which is why learning how it functions is exhilarating. With the right knowledge, you can make party combinations that laugh in the face of the game’s attempt at balance. Not that there is a lot of balance in SaGa Frontier, as bosses will routinely catch you unprepared and demolish you. But mastering the various mechanics in battle is fun when you can tinker and craft characters to become powerhouses, particularly with the vast array of potential builds at your disposal.

When SaGa Frontier is constrained, it’s at its weakest. There are some stories that feature extended segments where you are stuck in a location for reasons, preventing you from exploring the world. Elsewhere, you’ll be locked out of content if you unknowingly cross into an area that you didn’t know would remove certain characters or side quests from the map. And there aren’t a lot of side quests in SaGa Frontier – as delightful as it is to explore different areas, I do wish there were more activities that fleshed out the worlds themselves. As the dialogue is so perfunctory, I wished that there were more colour added to the game to fill in the gaps.

At the very least, many of the cracks found in the original release of SaGa Frontier have been repaired in the new remaster. This includes an eighth main character, Fuse, who sheds light on the narratives of the other seven main characters. There are also additional scenes for many of the existing stories; Asellus, in particular, has many new bits of dialogue that weren’t present in the original. And these additions are on top of improvements that make the remaster that much more playable like turbo speed modes for both exploration and combat, New Game+, and the ability to flee from every battle.

SaGa Frontier Remastered is a strange game to recommend. Odds are most people will bounce off of it because of its unconventional structure and commitment to explaining little. And yet it’s precisely because of its weird nature that I find it so compelling to play. SaGa Frontier Remastered is a perfect example of a cult classic, as there are only a few other games that are as unique and as polished as this.

notes.title: Notice regarding an issue occurring in SaGa Frontier Remastered
notes.content:
This is a notice regarding an issue which has been discovered in the Steam version of SaGa Frontier Remastered.

Currently there is a problem causing “save”, “autosave” and “quick save” to fail, we're looking into the cause behind this, and how to correct it.

We are incredibly sorry for any inconvenience this may cause, thank you for continuing to support SaGa Frontier Remastered.

notes.title: Одна из самых нелинейных JRPG: Обзор SaGa Frontier Remastered
notes.content: Square Enix продолжает свой крестовый поход по ностальгии, оживляя всё более нишевые серии. На этот раз нас чествуют ремастером SaGa Frontier - первой части дилогии Frontier с оригинальной PlayStation. Игры этой франшизы продолжают выходить, а отец серии Акитоси Кавадзу всё еще является сотрудником компании, что само по себе феномен, если учесть, сколько старых серий кануло в лету или попросту забыто, а разработчиков ушло на пенсию.

notes.title: SaGa Frontier Remastered is Out Now!
notes.content:
SaGa Frontier Remastered is out now! 

With optimised new features and graphics, an exciting new protagonist and never-before-seen content, the classic RPG title is now available on Steam.

Experience this role-playing adventure as one of eight heroes, each with their own storyline and goals, including exciting new protagonist FUSE. This remaster also features previously omitted scenarios and cutscenes, so you can delve deeper into the story than ever before!

Enjoy thrilling battles, and unfold your own unique story with the Free Scenario system.

The adventure is yours to explore!

notes.title: Pre-purchase SaGa Frontier Remastered
notes.content:
We're excited to announce that SaGa Frontier Remastered, is now available for pre-purchase on Steam! 

Experience this role-playing adventure as one of the eight heroes, each with their own storyline and goals. With the Free Scenario system, unfold your own unique journey.

Engage in dramatic battles, and use the Glimmer system to gain new skills and carry out combined attacks with your allies!

[h3]New Features Include:[/h3]
[b]・New Main Character, Fuse![/b]
The new main character, Fuse, can be played once certain conditions have been fulfilled. The Fuse scenario features great new tracks from Kenji Ito, and is full of new content. Discover a different side to the other main characters.

[b]・Phantom Cutscenes, Implemented at last[/b]
Several cutscenes that were cut have been added to Asellus's scenario. Delve deeper into the story than before.

[b]・Improved Graphics and Extensive New Features[/b]
Alongside upgraded high-resolution graphics, the UI has been updated and improved. Additional new features have been added, including double-speed mode, making gameplay smoother than ever. 

SaGa Frontier Remastered is available 15th April, 4pm UTC.
